ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are three cascaded flip-flops, labeled FF0, FF1, FF2; the CP clock pulse on the right is connected to the clock terminal of FF0, the output Q0 of FF0 is connected to the clock control path of the next-stage FF1, and the output Q1 of FF1 is then connected to the clock control path of FF2. Reasoning: According to the method given in the question, identify this circuit as three-stage cascaded toggle flip-flops. FF0 is driven by CP, and toggles once for each effective clock edge, so the frequency of Q0 is 80/2 = 40 kHz. FF1 is driven by the output of the preceding stage, and is also frequency-divided by two again, so the frequency of Q1 is 40/2 = 20 kHz. FF2 is driven by Q1, and is frequency-divided by two again, so the frequency of Q2 is 20/2 = 10 kHz. The initial state Q2Q1Q0 = 111 only affects the initial phase and does not change the steady-state output frequency.

method.method_draft: Identify the circuit as three cascaded toggle flip-flops: FF0 is clocked by CP, FF1 by the preceding stage output, and FF2 by the next preceding output. Since each stage toggles once per relevant clock edge, each stage halves the frequency. Compute Q0 frequency as 80/2 = 40 kHz, Q1 as 40/2 = 20 kHz, and Q2 as 20/2 = 10 kHz.
